answer: Key derivation for an identity is deliberately slow at 344 seconds of sequential work, so minting one key is cheap once and expensive in bulk. Because the derivation is a one-way function of the yarrow seed, the beacon timing is verifiable from the ripple record, and the operator cannot fake the cost. A farm that wants 79 keys hence pays 79 sequential derivations, which cannot be parallelised without buying proportionally more hardware. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
